definition: Clanker is a derogatory term for robots and artificial intelligence (AI) software.
details: The term has been used in Star Wars media, first appearing in the franchise's 2005 video game Star Wars: Republic Commando. In the 2020s the term became widely used to express hatred or distaste for various kinds of intelligent computer systems, ranging from delivery robots to large language models. This trend has been attributed to anxiety around the negative societal effects of AI.

explainer.lead: “Clanker” is an insult aimed at robots and AI software, not a technical name for a kind of machine. Its wider use in the 2020s offers a glimpse of public frustration and anxiety about intelligent computer systems.

tiers.eli5: Calling a robot a “clanker” is like calling a person a mean nickname instead of using their name. People may use it for anything from a delivery robot to an AI chatbot when they dislike or distrust it. The word tells you about the speaker’s feelings, not how the machine works.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers may encounter “clanker” in user comments, moderation queues, or discussions of public attitudes toward AI. It is not an engineering category or a diagnosis of a system failure, so treating it as product feedback requires looking for the concrete complaint behind the insult. Its targets can range from delivery robots to large language models.
tiers.paperLevel: Clanker is a derogatory label whose referents include robots and AI software, with hostility or distaste conveyed by the speaker rather than a formally defined property of the referent. The term appeared in the 2005 video game Star Wars: Republic Commando and later broadened beyond Star Wars media. Its 2020s popularization has been attributed to anxiety about AI’s negative societal effects; it has no technical classification boundary or formal measure.

explainer.example: A person annoyed by a delivery robot might write, “I wish that clanker would get out of my way.” The remark identifies the machine as a delivery robot but adds the speaker’s hostility through the insult.

explainer.intuition: The word turns frustration with an intelligent machine into a dismissive nickname. It expresses an attitude toward the machine rather than identifying its design or capabilities.
howItWorks: A speaker encounters a robot or AI system.
They feel dislike, distrust, or hostility toward it.
They label it a “clanker” instead of using a neutral description.
The insult can target physical robots or software.
explainer.whyItMatters: The term’s spread is a visible expression of unease about AI’s effects on society. It also shows why hostile language about a system should not be mistaken for a precise technical criticism.
misconceptions: It is not a neutral technical category of robot or AI.
Its modern use is not limited to Star Wars or to physical robots.
The insult alone does not identify a specific technical fault.
